newsitem.title: USA: US House will not kill ethanol tax break-Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: US House will not kill ethanol tax break-Gingrich.

text.p: A spokesperson for House Speaker Newt Gingrich Friday said the U.S. House of Representatives would not kill the ethanol tax break.
"The speaker has spoken with Archer, Nussle and others and we will solve the ethanol issue," said Gingrich spokesperson Christina Martin. "The House will not kill the ethanol provision."

House Ways and Means Committee chairman Bill Archer, Texas Republican, has proposed trimming the 5.4 cents per gallon tax break for ethanol users by a third of a cent and eliminating it in the year 2000.

On Thursday, the panel narrowly defeated an amendment by Rep. Jim Nussle, Iowa Republican, that would have retained tax subsidies for ethanol at present levels by cutting back on corporate capital gains tax relief.
Ethanol backers hope to quash the proposal to pare down the tax credit for the corn-based fuel when the tax bill goes to the full House for a vote, which is expected before the Fourth of July.
Two years ago, Gingrich, Georgia Republican, intervened in the final hour to save the ethanol subsidy from Archer's budget chopping block.
